stages.title: Email
stages.goal: Assess the email using evidence and extract indicators.
stages.output: Stage answers and an initial list of indicators.
stages.tools: Defang URL, From Base64, and URL Decode.
hints: Compare the displayed name with the actual address character by character.
The displayed link text is not necessarily the actual destination.
Use From Base64 or Defang URL in CyberChef on the link value.

stages.title: Logs
stages.goal: Build a timeline from multiple sources and identify affected accounts.
stages.output: A timeline table and a list of affected accounts.
stages.tools: Any spreadsheet application that opens CSV files.
hints: Sort events by time, not by file.
Look for an IP address appearing across multiple accounts.
GET retrieves the page; POST submits the data entered into it.

stages.title: Impact and Indicators
stages.goal: Determine what the attacker did, classify the impact using the CIA triad, and distinguish encoding, encryption, and hashing in practice.
stages.output: A CIA classification table, a comparison table, and decoded indicators.
stages.tools: From Base64, From Hex, XOR, and SHA2 (256-bit). Copy the kit identifier without trailing spaces or newlines, as these commonly cause hash mismatches.
hints: Read the audit log from top to bottom.
Base64-encoded URLs often begin with characters such as aHR0.
Hexadecimal text without a key may not be meaningful; look for the key in code comments.

stages.title: Response and Report
stages.goal: Make ordered, justified response decisions and summarize the incident like an analyst.
stages.output: A one-page incident report assessed using the rubric in the evaluation section.
hints: What is still happening and needs to be stopped now?
Do not delete evidence before preserving it.
Name each control alongside the vulnerability it addresses.
